external_research.title: What Does Activation Steering Control? Attribution Across Answer Encodings and Output-Sensitive Subspaces
external_research.authors: Zhiwei Gao, Shaowen Peng, Shoko Wakamiya, Eiji Aramaki
external_research.source_direct_finding: Cross-Encoding Steering Evaluation freezes an intervention while answer identifiers are re-encoded for the same held-out items. Reported experiments show that steering effects can follow the extraction index rather than the semantic label under the remapped encoding, and that a gain under one encoding does not by itself identify what the intervention controls.
external_research.project_implication: A Global J-Space/Hyperposition steering success under one output codebook cannot mint semantic causal-control credit. The intervention must survive preregistered answer-encoding remaps in a way that follows semantic identity rather than extraction index, answer-token identity, row position or codebook surface. METHOD_INPUT_ONLY; not Clay/Qwen-specific runtime evidence.

research_gap.existing_causal_law: Current Trigger-2 already separates decodability from actionability, uses bucketed causal evaluation, and separates local control from downstream update-path utilization.
research_gap.new_missing_distinction: Even an exact-site intervention with behavioral effect can control an output-sensitive encoding or extraction-index feature rather than the intended semantic state. Semantic attribution therefore requires cross-encoding invariance/equivariance tests in addition to intervention efficacy.
research_gap.why_nonduplicate: This gate asks what invariant the same frozen intervention follows after the answer representation is remapped. It is orthogonal to whether the signal is decodable, steerable, update-mediated, bucket-consistent, or low-collateral-damage.

hypothesis: A genuine semantic Global J-Space/Hyperposition control direction should preserve its declared semantic intervention effect when the same held-out task is expressed through preregistered alternative opaque answer encodings, after accounting for the explicitly allowed codebook transformation.
counterhypothesis: A strong intervention effect under the construction encoding is already sufficient evidence of semantic control; remapping answer identifiers merely adds cosmetic variation.
counterhypothesis_reason: The new cross-encoding evidence demonstrates a concrete alternative mechanism: the intervention can follow extraction index rather than semantic label. Therefore single-encoding success is not identifiable as semantic control.

hard_negative_blueprints_only.case: The frozen intervention strongly shifts the intended class under the construction encoding, but after a semantic-to-identifier permutation the effect stays attached to the original extraction index.
The intervention effect follows one answer token or opaque ABI atom across semantic remapping rather than following the semantic target.
Cross-encoding semantic following passes, but path-specific mediation shows the candidate state is not consumed by the intended recurrent update computation.

training_implication.positive_label_rule: Do not create a positive SEMANTIC_JSPACE_CONTROL or equivalent label from a steering gain measured under only one answer encoding.
training_implication.future_candidate_pairing: When executable evidence permits row generation, pair semantic-preserving codebook remaps with extraction-index-following and answer-token-following hard negatives so the model cannot learn that any intervention-induced output change proves semantic causality.
training_implication.architecture_relation: This gate is especially relevant to episode-local BIND_ROUTE plus WRITE behavior in variable-N HCU cognition because opaque ABI/codebook symbols are transport surfaces, not semantic authorities.

artifact_lifecycle_delta.revision_reason: No contradiction. Cross-encoding attribution adds a semantic-identifiability axis to the existing checkpoint controllability states.
Cross-encoding attribution and downstream utilization are independent gates: one asks what the intervention controls, the other asks whether the intended update path consumes it.
This research delta does not lift the existing model-visible nuisance leakage block.
